newsitem.title: FRANCE: French parliament to hold budget debate in Spring.
newsitem.headline: French parliament to hold budget debate in Spring.

text.p: France's parliament will get a chance to outline its wishes for the 1998 budget in a debate to be held this spring, a French minister said on Thursday.
It will be a repeat exercise of a spring debate held for the first time in both houses last May, which the government says provided groundwork for the 1997 budget unveiled in the autumn.
"Parliament will have the opportunity to discuss the main budgetary themes, in the form of a debate similar to last year, in Spring," parliamentary affairs minister Roger Romani said.
"You remember that debate very much inspired the govermnent in the preparation of the budget," he said.

Last year it used the debate to seek parliamentary support for deep cutbacks in public spending to help reduce its deficit in order to meet Maastricht Treaty deficit criteria in order to join a planned single European currency in 1999.
